messages:
maya: heads up — p99 spiked in yul around 09:12 UTC, affecting small requests (short prompts). Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/board/YUL-pop — latency jump ~150ms -> 420ms
oli: saw it too, started ~09:10. traceroute shows an extra hop via carrier-edge and a DNS rewrite at the provider (NXDOMAIN -> rewrite). cc @lee for kernel selector impact
lee: digging into selector traces now. initial read: kernel selection is oscillating when batch sizes hit 6–12. suspecting a KV cache warmup spike based on miss rates
jordan: metrics: kv_cache.warmup_miss_rate jumped from 0.12 -> 0.68 during the window. also backlog of tiny batches increased concurrency and forced different kernel path
maya: putting sample logs here:```
[2026-03-18T09:11:58Z] request id=abc123 batch_size=3 kernel=fast-path selected=1
[2026-03-18T09:12:02Z] request id=def456 batch_size=9 kernel=fallback selected=0 kv_hit=false
[2026-03-18T09:12:05Z] request id=ghi789 batch_size=2 kernel=fast-path selected=1 kv_hit=false
```
lee: profiler snapshot:```
kernel_selector.profiles: select_count=2412 fallback_count=198 avg_select_latency_ms=0.82 batch_size_hist={1:1200,6:512,9:400,16:300}
runtime.kv_cache: hit_rate=0.56 warmup_miss_rate=0.68 kv_lookup_ms_p50=0.9
```
oli: provider confirmed a DNS rewrite change in their edge that rewrites unknown subdomains to a proxy for analytics — introduces ~25–40ms extra RTT and occasional NXDOMAIN bursts. That explains more cache churn and more tiny batches (clients retrying)
jordan: question — is the selector reacting to the added RTT and flipping kernels? can we add hysteresis or a simple debounce to avoid immediate kernel reselects on small transient latency bumps
lee: yes. current heuristic: pick kernel per-batch based on recent perf sample (window 100ms). I'll push a temporary raise of the hysteresis window to 500ms and force keep-last-kernel if batch_size < 8. Quick patch ready
maya: can you canary that to yul? we need to know if it reduces p99 without breaking throughput
lee: deploying canary now to 10% of hosts in yul. deploy-bot: started canary deploy lee/kernel-selector-hysteresis-500ms to yul (10%)
deploy-bot: canary complete — 10% hosts updated (09:28 UTC)
lee: early numbers look promising: p99 on canary hosts down from 420ms -> 180ms, kv warmup miss reduced ~30% on canary. still seeing tail on non-canary hosts
maya: if stable for 15m, roll to 50% then full. Also contacting provider ops to rollback DNS rewrite or ask for rate-limited redirects
oli: provider ops responding — they rolled an emergency rule for the rewrite at 09:35 and are throttling analytics redirect traffic. they say a full revert takes 2h for config propagation
jordan: follow-up: need an RCA action item — kernel selector should be robust to sudden RTT increases from infra changes (provider-side). Add tests in perf-infra to simulate DNS-added-RTT + KV miss surge and verify hysteresis prevents oscillation
lee: filed perf ticket: PERF-1428 "selector hysteresis + kv warmup resilience" with test harness notes and links to traces
sre-bot: incident created INC-2026-0318-yul-dns-rewrite-kvcache, severity=info, owners=[lee,maya,oli]
maya: summary: cause=provider DNS rewrite causing extra RTT & NXDOMAIN bursts -> kv cache warmup -> increased tiny-batch churn -> kernel selector oscillation -> p99 spike. mitigation=selector hysteresis canary + provider throttled rewrite. next=perf tests + postmortem in 24h
oli: thumbs up :thumbsup: — keep thread updated if anything regresses
